sources.title: M. Talha Çiçek, The tribal partners of empire in Arabia: the Ottomans and the Rashidis of Najd, 1880 to 1918
sources.note: New Perspectives on Turkey 56 (2017), direct full HTML. Partnership and pilgrimage economy sections checked against their specific archive citations. Do not repeat the article’s inconsistent al-Hasa 1912/1913 date or statement identifying Ibn Saud’s father as Basra governor.

sources.title: Saudipedia, Unification of Saudi Arabia
sources.note: Direct institutional chronology, 1891 end of Second Saudi State and 1902 return to Riyadh. Reused source: existing Arabia (Nejd) card attributes 157 words to this work, leaving 43 words. This packet uses only a short chronology passage.

sources.title: Madawi al-Rasheed, A History of Saudi Arabia: The emerging state, 1902 to 1932
sources.note: Cambridge University Press, 2010 edition, chapter 2, pp. 37 to 68. Direct publisher summary checked: 1902 Riyadh capture, existing Rashidi authority, state-building and World War I as turning point. Only summary-supported claims used.

sources.title: Lady Anne Blunt, A Pilgrimage to Nejd, volume I, 1881
sources.note: Direct full transcription of second edition, based on 1878 to 1879 journey. Printed pp. 209, 219, 255 to 256 checked. Original Roman transcription and English translation preserved; no Arabic-script reconstruction. Cultural and racial rankings and speculative political generalizations rejected.

sources.title: J. G. Lorimer, Gazetteer of the Persian Gulf, volume II, 1908: Riyadh
sources.note: British Library IOR/L/PS/20/C91/4, printed p. 1593, indexed full original. Well depths, date-grove irrigation, trade and marble coffee mortars. Gazetteer compiles reports; not all details were directly observed by Lorimer. Group all volume pages and editions of this same account for budgets.

sources.title: Gertrude Bell, diary entry of 7 March 1914, Ha’il
sources.note: Newcastle University, GB/2/13/2/3/7. Direct full archive transcription: women dairy sellers and palace photography. Evidence at the imported endpoint is explicitly dated. Group all Bell 1914 Ha’il diaries and associated letters conservatively. Lexical gloss semneh as clarified butter additionally checked in FAO https://www.fao.org/4/y0600m/y0600m06.htm; no modern production practice transferred into historical claim.

sources.title: Gertrude Bell, diary written for Charles Doughty-Wylie, 2 March 1914
sources.note: Newcastle University, GB/2/15/3/1. Direct full original diary transcription. Lu.lu.ah caretaker and enslaved woman with her son, former summer palace and unwatered gardens. Public copy avoids unsupported assumptions about kinship, property rights or all women’s circumstances.

sources.title: Guido Steinberg, Ecology, Knowledge, and Trade in Central Arabia
sources.note: EUI working-paper version, printed p. 13, indexed original full passage on financial support and leaving school for commerce/agriculture. Broad nineteenth/early twentieth-century scope; later 1940 and disability generalizations excluded. Group with existing Arabia (Nejd) study and FU Berlin epidemic essay conservatively.

sources.title: Musée du Louvre, Stèle de Teima, AO 1505
sources.note: Full indexed museum catalogue directly checked via query Stèle de Teima 1884 Louvre; direct open failed. Catalogue dates object to fifth century BCE, discovery in house reuse in 1884, acquisition 1885; language and script Aramaic. Do not use older sixth-century dating from museum-shop replica listing.

sources.title: British Library, Lady Anne Blunt’s Nejd sketchbook, Add MS 54048
sources.note: Direct original archive catalogue, date span 13 December 1878 to 20 February 1879. Supports survival of separately catalogued sketchbook, not detailed image contents that have not been viewed.

proposedOverrides.summary: Late nineteenth-century Arabian interior communities, Saudi and Rashidi rivalry, oasis crafts, households and trade.

batchIdentityNotes.decision: One exact indexed record, 1878 to 1914, no aliases.
batchIdentityNotes.geometry: Three near-identical snapshots 1878 to 1880, 1880 to 1900 and 1900 to 1914. Main scope spans northern, central and broad southern interior. Public overview names included and excluded reference points and rejects unified political interpretation.
batchIdentityNotes.related: Do not merge ancient Arabian pastoral nomads, Arabs, Saba, nejd (1783 to 1878), arabia-nejd (1914 to 1920), modern Saudi Arabia or coastal/neighboring states.
batchIdentityNotes.writing: Specific 1879 speech preserved in the 1881 Blunt printed Roman transcription with her English translation. No reconstructed Arabic script; not represented as an indigenous written artifact.
batchIdentityNotes.limits: No securely dated toilet feature established; well evidence is not a sewer claim. Bell observations are explicitly at 1914 endpoint. Ancient Tayma artifact is included only as an 1884 discovery, with ancient date and language separated.
